header.title: GEM Strategy
header.subtitle: Global equities momentum – equities versus a safe asset
header.explainer: Global Equities Momentum allocates the whole strategy portfolio to a single asset each period: equities when their {months}-month return beats the risk-free asset (absolute momentum), otherwise the safe asset. Among equities, the market with the strongest {months}-month return wins (relative momentum).

scenarios.createHint: A second scenario lets you run the same rules another way — a shorter momentum window, a quarterly cadence, a different set of instruments — and compare them once both have evaluated.
scenarios.createError: The scenario could not be created.
scenarios.deleteMessage: {name} will be removed with its role assignments and its whole evaluation history. The history cannot be rebuilt: it records the momentum figures each past decision was taken on.
scenarios.deleteError: The scenario could not be deleted.

stale.updating: Updating — the figures below are from the previous selection

roleDescriptions.US_EQUITY: US large caps. Its return is the one the absolute-momentum test measures against the risk-free benchmark.
roleDescriptions.EX_US_EQUITY: Developed markets outside the US — Europe, Japan, Canada, Australia. Competes with the other two equity legs in the ranking.
roleDescriptions.EM_EQUITY: Emerging markets — China, India, Taiwan, Brazil and the rest. Competes with the other two equity legs in the ranking.
roleDescriptions.SAFE: Held while RISK-OFF (e.g. an aggregate bond ETF).
roleDescriptions.RISK_FREE: Optional. The yardstick the absolute-momentum test measures equities against (e.g. T-bills). Left empty, the safe asset is used.

chart.title: Asset performance – {window}
chart.hint: Cumulative total return of every asset used to determine the signal, rebased to zero at the start of the window.
chart.noDataDescription: None of the strategy assets has prices for this window. Import or refresh prices to see the comparison.
chart.footnote: Total return of each instrument in its own listing currency — the same basis the signal is decided on. A currency move between them is not included.

chart.currentPortfolioNote: The simulation applies today’s instrument proportions at the start of the selected period. It does not reproduce historical transactions, cash flows, cash or currency movements.
chart.currentPortfolioLateStart: The simulation starts later because at least one of the instruments you hold now has no data from the start of the selected period.
chart.currentPortfolioEarlyEnd: The simulation stops on {date}, because {symbols} has no prices after that date — refresh its price history to draw the rest.

currentPortfolioUnavailable.NO_HOLDINGS: The strategy accounts hold no instruments, so there is no portfolio to simulate.
currentPortfolioUnavailable.UNKNOWN_CURRENT_VALUE: One of the instruments held has no current value, so today’s proportions are unknown and the simulation is not shown.
currentPortfolioUnavailable.MISSING_PRICE_HISTORY: One of the instruments held has no usable price history, so the simulation is not shown: a line drawn from the rest would be a different portfolio.

allocation.title: Strategy allocation
allocation.hint: The target weights the current signal implies.
allocation.ruleTwoSteps: Two decisions: absolute then relative momentum
allocation.noSignalDescription: The allocation appears once the strategy produces a signal.

reasoning.title: Why this signal?
reasoning.hint: The two decisions behind the current allocation, with the figures they were taken on.
reasoning.riskOffExplainer: The strategy is RISK-OFF, so the equity ranking does not affect the current allocation.
reasoning.leadUnknown: The lead over second place is not available.
reasoning.noRankingDescription: Assign instruments to the equity roles to rank them.
reasoning.noSignalDescription: The two decision steps appear once the strategy has been evaluated.
reasoning.step1Question: Stay in equities, or move to bonds?
reasoning.step1AnswerRiskOn: {equity} ({equityReturn}) came out ahead of {benchmark} ({benchmarkReturn}), so the strategy stays in equities.
reasoning.step1AnswerRiskOff: {equity} ({equityReturn}) did not come out ahead of {benchmark} ({benchmarkReturn}), so the strategy moves to the safe asset {safe}.
reasoning.step2QuestionSkipped: Which equity market? Not asked this period
reasoning.step2Answer: {winner} had the strongest return ({winnerReturn}), so that market is the target for this period.
reasoning.step2Skipped: This step is not applied: the first decision already moved the strategy to {safe}, so the ranking changes nothing this period.
reasoning.thresholdRiskOn: The signal moves to bonds once {equity}’s return falls below {benchmark}’s.
reasoning.thresholdRiskOff: The signal returns to equities once {equity}’s return rises above {benchmark}’s.
reasoning.thresholdUnknown: The margin cannot be shown without a {months}-month return for both instruments.

history.title: Signal history

history.emptyDescription: Past signals appear here after the strategy's first evaluation.

portfolioPanel.title: Strategy position
portfolioPanel.holdingsHint: Everything held in these accounts counts: the strategy wants all of it in the target instrument, so a holding outside the strategy has to be moved too.
portfolioPanel.workingCashNote: Uninvested — counts towards nothing and funds the purchase
portfolioPanel.workingUnknown: The share cannot be worked out until the holdings can be priced.
portfolioPanel.basisComposition: Exposure is estimated from what each instrument holds, compared by {dimension}. It is an estimate beside the allocation, not part of it: only the target instrument itself counts as holding the target.
portfolioPanel.basisInstrument: Market exposure cannot be estimated, because {target} has no {dimension} structure recorded in Monize. Compliance with the signal is still calculated exactly, by instrument.
portfolioPanel.basisPartialData: {count, plural, one {# holding has} other {# holdings have}} no structure recorded, so the estimate for the portfolio is unavailable.
portfolioPanel.partialMatch: {percent} estimated exposure to the target market
portfolioPanel.noPositionHint: The strategy accounts hold no instruments yet.
portfolioPanel.workingExposure: Estimated exposure to the target market
portfolioPanel.workingFloorNote: Where a fund's breakdown covers only part of it, the exposure is shown as a lower bound: the markets it does not name may add to it.
portfolioPanel.workingSum: {counted} of the {total} held in instruments is in the target instrument, which is the {percent} above.
portfolioPanel.basisFillStructure: Fill in the instrument’s geographic structure

backtest.title: Backtest
backtest.hint: Simulated results for the configured asset set.
backtest.netOfCosts: Figures are net of estimated taxes and commissions.
backtest.netOfTaxOnly: Figures are net of estimated taxes, but not of commissions.
backtest.netOfCommissionOnly: Figures are net of estimated commissions, but not of taxes.
backtest.partialCoverage: Prices cover only the most recent {coverage} of the evaluated periods, so the simulation starts there. Everything before the last period that could not be priced is left out of the figures above, and costs are excluded because a run starting mid-strategy has no purchase price to tax.
backtest.emptyDescription: A backtest needs full price history for every strategy asset. Once it exists, its summary appears here.

settingsForm.assetsHint: Assign an ETF or fund to each role. The strategy produces its first signal once the US equity leg and the safe asset both have an instrument with {months} months of prices.
settingsForm.accountsHint: Holdings are summed across every account you pick.
settingsForm.fillMissing: Add {count, plural, one {the missing instrument} other {the # missing instruments}}
settingsForm.fillMissingHint: Never bought an instrument for these roles? Add the ETFs GEM is usually run with ({symbols}). Saving the configuration loads their price history and evaluates the first signal. You can point any role at a different instrument first.
settingsForm.fillMissingDone: {count, plural, one {# instrument added} other {# instruments added}}. Save the configuration to load their prices and evaluate the first signal.
settingsForm.fillMissingError: Could not add the suggested instruments.
settingsForm.rulesSourceUrl: Link to the rules you follow
settingsForm.rulesSourceLabel: Text to show for that link
settingsForm.rulesSourceHint: Both optional, and neither affects any calculation. They put a link in the report footer to wherever the rules this strategy follows are written down — an article, a book page, your own notes — so you can check later which version you set it up against.
settingsForm.saveError: Could not save the strategy configuration.
settingsForm.lookupsError: Your accounts and instruments could not be loaded, so the settings cannot be edited safely.
settingsForm.addInstrumentPrefilled: Filled in from the suggested listing. Change the exchange and currency to the ones your broker actually trades.
settingsForm.currencyHint: Try to keep every instrument in one currency: the strategy holds one of them at a time and moves the whole position on each switch, so a mixed set pays a conversion every move.
settingsForm.currencyMixed: The assigned instruments span {currencies}. The strategy converts the whole position on every switch between them; one currency throughout avoids that cost.
